headline.caveat: bilateral credit line — OpenAI's first from a single bank

realized_to_date.caveat: drawn amount undisclosed; a line, not a funded term loan

nature_md: In mid-2026 Bank of America extended OpenAI a $520M bilateral credit line — the first single-bank loan to the company, and a reversal after BofA declined OpenAI's financing requests roughly a year earlier. Bloomberg framed the U-turn explicitly as relationship banking ahead of OpenAI's planned US IPO (confidentially filed; >$1T valuation targeted per Reuters): early lending buys visibility into cash needs and positions the bank for underwriting and advisory mandates at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Small in dollars by this dataset's standards, large as a signal — regulated bank balance sheets beginning to take direct, uncollateralized AI-lab credit exposure.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: For BofA: a loan commitment — undrawn portions are off-balance-sheet commitments (earning fees), drawn amounts become C&I loans. Adds to the banking system's AI-adjacent C&I exposure the Chicago Fed sized at ~25% of Tier 1 capital commitments.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: For OpenAI: drawn balances are debt; the facility diversifies liquidity away from equity megarounds and prepayments. Terms (pricing, covenants, security) undisclosed.

events.title: Bloomberg reports BofA's $520M credit line to OpenAI ahead of IPO
